items.title: stack: import an existing stack from a merge request
items.body:
### Problem

`glab stack` keeps its metadata only in the local `.git/stacked/`.
A stack created on another machine, or by a teammate, cannot be worked with locally.
`glab stack infer` builds a new stack from commits, but creates new branches, so `glab stack sync` would open duplicate merge requests.

### Proposal

`glab stack import <mr>` rebuilds the local stack metadata from GitLab:

1. From the given MR, follow `target_branch` down to the base branch, and follow MRs whose `target_branch` is the current `source_branch` up to the top.
2. Write one `StackRef` per MR (`prev`, `next`, `branch`, `mr`, `description`) plus `BASE_BRANCH`. For glab-named branches (`<prefix>-<title>-<sha>`), title and SHA come from the branch name; otherwise from flags or generated.
3. Create local branches tracking the remote ones and set the stack as current.

Afterwards `glab stack sync` updates the existing MRs instead of creating new ones.

### Open questions

- Several open MRs targeting the same branch: refuse or prompt?
- Support MRs from forks in the first version?

Writing these files by hand for an existing 5-MR stack worked: `glab stack list` showed it correctly.

items.title: glab mcp was removed
items.body:
Hello,

I read that glab mcp was deprecated and then removed

   https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8618

But it was very very useful and we cannot use the new http version: we have a managed gitlab installation and we do know when we can upgrade it to the version with mcp enabled.

In the meanwhile we'll keep an old GOOD version of "glab" and we'll stop upgrading the cli.

Thanks
Matteo

items.title: mr create --wip should behave the same as of mr create --draft
items.body:
### Problem to solve

When passing `--wip` to `mr create`, the resulting MR title will be prefixed with `WIP:`, which as far as I know is not very useful, as it has no special meaning to Gitlab, so I don't see any use case for `--wip`.

### Proposal

Passing `--wip` to `mr create` should prefix the MR title with `Draft:` instead of `WIP:`, as Draft has a meaning for Gitlab.

This mean that `--wip` should not be "an alternative" to `--draft`, instead, an alias.

Another possibility is to simply remove the `--wip` option completely to prevent confusion. Manually adding a `WIP:` to the MR title is simple enough not to need any special handling within the tool.
